stops.name: Ascona, Danses sacrées de l'Orient
stops.campa: The first light after the dark decade: Danses sacrées de l'Orient, the sacred dances of the East, at San Materno in 1950. She reopens with Jodjana's inheritance, the hand-language, the temple gestures, as though the way back to the Gothic led properly through Egypt, the route of the Holy Family reversed. The audiences are smaller, the shore quieter, the century elsewhere; none of it signifies. The theater relights on her own terms: dance as devotion, offered at intervals, to whom it concerns.

stops.name: Ascona: the wise and foolish virgins, with Olga Schwind
stops.campa: The true reopening, 1952: an evening of early music and medieval sacred dance with Olga Schwind of Ronco sopra Ascona, lutenist and organist of the old repertories: La resurrezione delle vergini stolte e sagge, the resurrection of the wise and foolish virgins, and La danza dei beati, the dance of the blessed, after Dante. Two women past the world's fashion restore the Middle Ages on a rationalist stage, exactly, unhurriedly, and the Asconesi remember it for decades: medieval dance made gesture full of enigmas.

stops.name: Ascona, the Easter liturgy of San Materno
stops.campa: Now the theater's calendar is the Church's: in the days before and after Easter she gives her sacred dances almost as a domestic liturgy, with small consorts of old instruments: vielle, portative organ, Minnesänger harp, pan flute, and amateur companions where needed. In 1955 she dances Zu Ehren von Fra' Angelico, in honor of Fra Angelico, to César Franck, and revives the Flight into Egypt. The gothic dancer has become what she always imitated: a fixed feast, a local rite, an image before which the faithful gather annually.
stops.quote: Dance is the most complete prayer, for the sense and the intensity of the gesture have no equal in the word
stops.quote_source: Bara on her sacred dances, recorded in the Dizionario della musica nella Svizzera italiana

stops.name: Ascona, the last dance
stops.campa: In July 1958 Charlotte Bara dances at San Materno for the last time. No abdication scene is recorded; the liturgy simply completes itself, thirty years almost to the season since the white theater opened. She is fifty-seven and has danced publicly for forty-one years: Brussels under occupation, Reinhardt's Berlin, the poet's lake, her own temple. The stage falls quiet; the school closes its register; the castle keeps her. The long evening of the dancer begins, which the canon counts not as silence but as stillness.

stops.name: Monte Verità: Szeemann's mountain, the elder witness
stops.campa: Harald Szeemann raises his great exhibition Monte Verità, le mammelle della verità, across Ascona, Casa Anatta and the Brissago islands, and sets Charlotte Bara among its exemplary artists: the hill's whole heresy curated as a total artwork, and the gothic dancer, seventy-seven and living below in her castle, entered into the museum of her own myth beside Laban and the barefoot prophets she outlived. The same year the theater passes to the commune of Ascona. She attends her own canonization with the composure of one who always knew the Gothic outlasts its century.

stops.name: Locarno, the death of the gothic dancer
stops.campa: She dies at Locarno on 7 December 1986, eighty-five years old, having lived out her days at San Materno among the drawings, programs and tunics of six decades. The obituaries reach back to the twenties to explain her; the lake needs no explanation, having kept her as a neighbor saint for sixty-six years. Of the great soloists of Ausdruckstanz she is among the last to go: the one who answered the century's ecstasies and catastrophes with a single sustained attitude of adoration.

stops.name: Ascona, the temple dances again
stops.campa: The afterlife of the temple: the canton lists Weidemeyer's white geometry among its protected monuments, the commune restores it with archaeological care, and the Teatro San Materno reopens as a working theater of dance. In 2007 her archive, more than two thousand four hundred photographs, letters and programs, enters the museums of Ascona; in 2018 Roberta Pedrini's film Le passioni di Charlotte carries her to the screens. A school of dance keeps term on the site once more; the twelve minutes the century lost in 1923 are thus, in kind, repaid.
